paragraphs.title: The Covenant of Love and David’s Success

easy.explanation: The verse says that Jonathan’s soul was knit with the soul of David.
easy.q: Whose soul was knit with David’s soul?

easy.explanation: Jonathan and David made a covenant because Jonathan loved David as his own soul.
easy.q: What did Jonathan and David make?

easy.explanation: Saul set David over the men of war.
easy.q: Over whom did Saul set David?

medium.explanation: Jonathan gave David his robe, garments, sword, bow, and girdle.
medium.q: What did Jonathan give David as a sign of his love?

medium.explanation: A covenant is a solemn and binding agreement between people.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “a covenant” mean in this passage?

answers: David behaved himself wisely wherever Saul sent him
David wanted to leave the army
medium.explanation: David behaved himself wisely and was accepted by the people and Saul’s servants.
medium.q: Why did Saul appoint David over the men of war?

answers: A relationship of loyalty and commitment
challenge.explanation: Jonathan’s love was demonstrated through a covenant and the giving of his clothing and weapons.
challenge.q: What kind of relationship is shown by Jonathan’s love, covenant, and gifts to David?

challenge.explanation: The passage shows that David’s wise conduct and success were recognized by many.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David being accepted by both the people and Saul’s servants?

answers: An increase in his responsibility and position
challenge.explanation: David moved from serving in Saul’s household to holding authority over the men of war.
challenge.q: What does David’s appointment over the men of war show?

easy.explanation: The women came out from all the cities of Israel with singing, dancing, tabrets, and instruments of musick.
easy.q: Who came out singing and dancing after David’s victory?

answers: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands
David hath slain his thousands, and Saul his ten thousands
easy.explanation: The women praised Saul for thousands but David for ten thousands.
easy.q: What did the women sing about Saul and David?

easy.explanation: Saul cast the javelin at David, intending to smite him to the wall.
easy.q: What did Saul throw at David?

medium.explanation: Saul was angry because the women credited David with ten thousands and Saul with only thousands.
medium.q: Why was Saul very wroth after hearing the women’s song?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes David as acting with wisdom and succeeding in his responsibilities.
medium.q: In the KJV context, what does “behaved himself wisely” mean?

answers: Removed David and made him captain over a thousand
medium.explanation: Saul removed David from his presence and made him captain over a thousand.
medium.q: What did Saul do after attempting to strike David with the javelin?

answers: Saul changed from love to support
Saul changed from approval to jealousy and hostility
Saul changed from indifference to friendship
challenge.explanation: Saul became angry, eyed David, and began to oppose him after hearing the song.
challenge.q: What change took place in Saul’s attitude toward David after the women’s song?

challenge.explanation: The passage directly says that Saul was afraid because the Lord was with David.
challenge.q: Why was Saul afraid of David?

answers: The people loved David, while Saul feared him
The people feared David, while Saul loved him
challenge.explanation: All Israel and Judah loved David, while Saul became afraid and hostile toward him.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the people and Saul in their response to David?

paragraphs.title: Saul’s Attempts to Bring About David’s Downfall

easy.explanation: Saul offered David his elder daughter Merab.
easy.q: Which daughter did Saul first offer to David as a wife?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Michal Saul’s daughter loved David.
David and his men slew two hundred Philistines.
easy.q: How many Philistines did David and his men kill?

answers: To keep David away from battle
To put David in danger before the Philistines
medium.explanation: Saul hoped that the hand of the Philistines would be against David.
medium.q: What did Saul hope to accomplish by giving David a daughter in marriage?

answers: A payment or gift connected with marriage
medium.explanation: Saul said he did not want a customary dowry, but instead demanded one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “dowry”?

answers: He went with his men and slew Philistines
medium.explanation: David and his men went out, slew Philistines, and brought their foreskins to Saul.
medium.q: What did David do after hearing Saul’s condition?

answers: It required David to leave his family
It connected the marriage with warfare against the Philistines
challenge.explanation: Saul used the marriage condition to expose David to danger in battle.
challenge.q: Why was Saul’s marriage proposal dangerous for David?

answers: He fulfilled the condition and exceeded it
challenge.explanation: Saul demanded one hundred, but David brought two hundred.
challenge.q: What does David bringing two hundred foreskins show?

answers: Saul turned to Michal and viewed her as a snare for David
Saul sent David away in peace
challenge.explanation: Saul planned to use Michal’s love for David to place him in danger.
challenge.q: How did Saul’s plan change after Merab was not given to David?

paragraphs.title: David Rises as Saul Becomes His Enemy

answers: The Lord had departed from David
easy.explanation: Saul saw and knew that the Lord was with David.
easy.q: What did Saul recognize about the Lord and David?

easy.explanation: Saul knew that Michal, his daughter, loved David.
His name was much set by, meaning that David was highly regarded.

answers: Saul saw that the Lord was with David and that Michal loved him
medium.explanation: Both David’s divine favor and Michal’s love increased Saul’s fear.
medium.q: Why did Saul become even more afraid of David?

answers: David succeeded and acted more wisely than Saul’s other servants
David stayed alone in his house
medium.explanation: David showed greater wisdom and success than all the other servants of Saul.
medium.q: What does “behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul” mean?

medium.explanation: The passage says that Saul became David’s enemy continually.
medium.q: What did Saul become after recognizing that the Lord was with David?

answers: Michal’s love increased Saul’s fear of David
Michal’s love caused Saul to love David
challenge.explanation: Saul saw both Michal’s love for David and David’s success, which increased his fear.
challenge.q: What was the connection between Michal’s love for David and Saul’s fear?

answers: He repeatedly succeeded and surpassed Saul’s servants
challenge.explanation: David behaved more wisely than all Saul’s servants whenever the Philistine princes went forth.
challenge.q: What does the ending emphasize about David’s success in battle?

answers: David weakened while Saul grew stronger
David rose in honor while Saul became his enemy
challenge.explanation: David continued to succeed and gain honor, while Saul’s fear and hostility increased.
challenge.q: What process is described in verses 28–30?
